correctness.rationale: Fourier invertibility uses the existence of all exponent roots and invertibility of |G|. Raising the inverse Fourier sum to q proves descent. The nonzero support is forward-invariant under A,B and, by finiteness, also invariant under their inverses; Frobenius preserves it. On each orbit the logarithmic equations give the stated integer matrix, whose unimodular Smith reductions are valid modulo N even when N is composite or 1. The trivial character gives two independent choices, splitting the augmentation counts. The original midpoint proof asserted q^s−2^h is prime to the characteristic; this is false, e.g. G=C3 and q=2 with r=2,s=h=1, where it is zero. The repair proves consistency and g=gcd(2^r−1,q^s−2^h) divides N: F^L=1 implies s|L and r|hL/s, so q^L≡2^(hL/s)≡1 mod g. The cyclic splitting-field group therefore contains exactly g allowed nonzero parameters, including the example with g=3. The characteristic-two midpoint coefficient count follows separately from cancellation of off-diagonal terms and basis idempotency. All formulas and hypotheses are unchanged.
residual_risks: General correctness rests on the algebraic proof; the source's reported small enumerations are not a certificate for arbitrary groups.

value.rationale: The exact classification of these algebra idempotents gives actual elements and counts for variable finite groups and fields without searching coefficient vectors. Handling nonscalar connected actions and nonsplitting fields is essential to that uniformity, and the midpoint gcd makes the twist explicit rather than extrapolating from splitting or dihedral examples.
